excerpt: You can create a Linux machine using the Paperspace console, Paperspace API, or Paperspace CLI.
You can connect to your Linux or Windows-based machine using the Paperspace console or desktop app using SSH connection.
Custom templates are templates of your machines and their configurations. You can use these custom templates to create new machines with your specifications.
Shared drives provide storage that is accessible from multiple machines in a private network.
The auto-shutdown feature places your machine in a stop state after a predefined period of inactivity, which can range from one hour to one week.
API keys let you interact with Paperspace through the Core RESTful API, the Core JavaScript SDK, and Gradient command-line utility (CLI).
Notebooks are a web-based Jupyter IDE with shared persistent storage for long-term development and inter-notebook collaboration, backed by accelerated compute.
Deployments are containers-as-a-service that let you run container images and serve machine learning models.
Workflows automate machine learning tasks, combining GPU instances with an expressive syntax to generate production-ready machine learning pipelines with a few lines of code.

The gaming community also used Paperspace sometimes for PC game streaming, installing Steam to tap into existing libraries; used it on vacation to play Assassin's Creed Odyssey and it worked pretty well.

Paperspace gives free access to Graphcore IPU nodes (4 IPUs each)... But in practice, I tore my hair out trying to port Stable Diffusion web UI, hit a wall needing to upgrade Poplar SDK behind a corporate login. That left a bad taste in my mouth.
Oh, fun memories - locked me out of my account (froze it or whatnot) but happily charged me. Didn't notice for a while as I didn't really use it. Support just ignored my questions.
Back when I was in college Paperspace was kind enough to give us a few thousand in compute credits for our research project around autonomous driving to help with training costs.
I use Stable Diffusion with Paperspace's Pro tier ($9/mo) which gives you up to 6 hours of non per-usage GPU... My worry is that plan will go away replaced by strict per usage costs.
PaperSpace product recently has been really bad. Gradient Notebooks are a worse version of Google Colab. Useless for any serious DL product building.

Their DL virtual servers (Core) are horrible. Very slow internet, takes forever to copy datasets. Most of the time it's an uphill battle to get ssh access; they create a pointless virtual console instead of simple ssh access.
Once I discovered Lambda and Vast.ai, I never looked back and forgot Paperspace for good.
I use a paperspace VM + Parsec for personal ML projects. An hourly rate on a standard VM w/GPU is better than purchasing a local machine; as a bonus you can re-use these VMs for hobby gaming too.
Man I had such a problem using paper space's notebook system, that I just gave up. In retrospect it was more to do with me not understanding generator functions for memory bloating.
paper space has such an oddball product - they first started off as some sort of cloud Virtual Desktop type of thing and this seems to be their new pivot.
